1	"""
2	Credential resolution for scrapers.
3	
4	Order of resolution for a provider like "amex":
5	  1. Direct env vars: AMEX_USERNAME and AMEX_PASSWORD
6	  2. Cached JSON dump:  ~/.argus/bw_cache/<provider>.json  (or whatever
7	     AMEX_BW_ITEM points to). Use this when `bw` subprocess calls hang
8	     (known macOS keychain issue). Refresh with:
9	         bw get item amex --session "$BW_SESSION" > ~/.argus/bw_cache/amex.json
10	  3. Bitwarden CLI: looks up item named "amex" (override with AMEX_BW_ITEM).
11	     Requires BW_SESSION to be set. To get one:
12	         export BW_SESSION="$(bw unlock --raw)"
13	
14	Supported Bitwarden item types:
15	  - Login (type 1): returns (login.username, login.password)
16	  - Card  (type 3): returns (card.number, custom_field "passcode")
17	                    The passcode field on a Card item is the CVV (3-4 digits),
18	                    not the online banking passcode — so the latter must live
19	                    in a custom field. Add one named exactly "passcode".
20	
21	Returns (username, password) or (None, None) if nothing resolved.
22	"""
23	
24	import json
25	import os
26	import subprocess
27	from pathlib import Path
28	
29	BW_CACHE_DIR = Path.home() / ".argus" / "bw_cache"
30	
31	BW_TYPE_LOGIN = 1
32	BW_TYPE_CARD = 3
33	
34	
35	def get_credentials(provider: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
36	    upper = provider.upper()
37	
38	    u = os.environ.get(f"{upper}_USERNAME")
39	    p = os.environ.get(f"{upper}_PASSWORD")
40	    if u and p:
41	        return u, p
42	
43	    item_name = os.environ.get(f"{upper}_BW_ITEM", provider)
44	
45	    cached = _from_cache(provider, item_name)
46	    if cached is not None:
47	        return _extract(cached)
48	
49	    return _from_bitwarden(item_name)
50	
51	
52	def get_card(provider: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
53	    """Return (card_number, cvv) for a provider's Card item in Bitwarden."""
54	    session = os.environ.get("BW_SESSION")
55	    if not session:
56	        return None, None
57	    item_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider.upper()}_BW_CARD_ITEM", provider)
58	    items = _bw_run(["bw", "list", "items", "--search", item_name, "--session", session])
59	    if not isinstance(items, list):
60	        return None, None
61	    cards = [i for i in items if i.get("type") == BW_TYPE_CARD]
62	    if not cards:
63	        return None, None
64	    exact = [i for i in cards if (i.get("name") or "").strip() == item_name]
65	    card = (exact or cards)[0].get("card") or {}
66	    return card.get("number"), card.get("code")
67	
68	
69	def _from_bitwarden(item_name: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
70	    """Try direct lookup; if ambiguous, fall back to search + filter by type.
71	    Prefers Login items over Card items."""
72	    session = os.environ.get("BW_SESSION")
73	    if not session:
74	        return None, None
75	
76	    direct = _bw_run(["bw", "get", "item", item_name, "--session", session])
77	    if isinstance(direct, dict):
78	        return _extract(direct)
79	
80	    items = _bw_run(["bw", "list", "items", "--search", item_name, "--session", session])
81	    if not isinstance(items, list) or not items:
82	        return None, None
83	
84	    # Prefer Login type over Card type — within each, prefer exact name match.
85	    for wanted in (BW_TYPE_LOGIN, BW_TYPE_CARD):
86	        by_type = [i for i in items if i.get("type") == wanted]
87	        if not by_type:
88	            continue
89	        exact = [i for i in by_type if (i.get("name") or "").strip() == item_name]
90	        return _extract((exact or by_type)[0])
91	
92	    return None, None
93	
94	
95	def _extract(item: dict) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
96	    t = item.get("type")
97	    if t == BW_TYPE_LOGIN:
98	        login = (item.get("login") or {})
99	        return login.get("username"), login.get("password")
100	    if t == BW_TYPE_CARD:
101	        card = (item.get("card") or {})
102	        return card.get("number"), _custom_field(item, "passcode")
103	    return None, None
104	
105	
106	def _bw_run(cmd: list[str]) -> dict | list | None:
107	    debug = os.environ.get("BW_DEBUG")
108	    try:
109	        result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
110	    except FileNotFoundError:
111	        if debug:
112	            print(f"  [bw] FileNotFoundError — is `bw` on PATH? ({cmd[0]})")
113	        return None
114	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
115	        if debug:
116	            print(f"  [bw] timeout: {' '.join(cmd[:4])}")
117	        return None
118	    if result.returncode != 0:
119	        if debug:
120	            print(f"  [bw] exit {result.returncode}: {result.stderr.strip()[:200]}")
121	        return None
122	    try:
123	        return json.loads(result.stdout)
124	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
125	        if debug:
126	            print(f"  [bw] non-JSON stdout: {result.stdout[:200]}")
127	        return None
128	
129	
130	def _norm(s: str | None) -> str:
131	    return "".join(c.lower() for c in (s or "") if c.isalnum())
132	
133	
134	def _custom_field(item: dict, name: str) -> str | None:
135	    target = _norm(name)
136	    for field in (item.get("fields") or []):
137	        if _norm(field.get("name")) == target:
138	            return field.get("value")
139	    return None
140	
141	
142	def get_custom_field(provider: str, field_name: str) -> str | None:
143	    """Look up a Bitwarden custom field on any item matching the provider name.
144	    Field-name match is fuzzy: ignores case, spaces, underscores, hyphens."""
145	    item_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider.upper()}_BW_ITEM", provider)
146	
147	    cached = _from_cache(provider, item_name)
148	    if cached is not None:
149	        val = _custom_field(cached, field_name)
150	        if val:
151	            return val
152	
153	    session = os.environ.get("BW_SESSION")
154	    if not session:
155	        return None
156	    items = _bw_run(["bw", "list", "items", "--search", item_name, "--session", session])
157	    if not isinstance(items, list):
158	        return None
159	    for wanted in (BW_TYPE_LOGIN, BW_TYPE_CARD):
160	        for item in items:
161	            if item.get("type") != wanted:
162	                continue
163	            val = _custom_field(item, field_name)
164	            if val:
165	                return val
166	    return None
167	
168	
169	def _from_cache(provider: str, item_name: str) -> dict | None:
170	    """Read a Bitwarden item from ~/.argus/bw_cache/. Tries provider name,
171	    item_name, and sanitized variants."""
172	    candidates = [provider, item_name, item_name.replace(".", "_")]
173	    for name in candidates:
174	        path = BW_CACHE_DIR / f"{name}.json"
175	        if path.exists():
176	            try:
177	                return json.loads(path.read_text())
178	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
179	                continue
180	    return None
181	
```

  "new_string": "    # Wait for the Midata disclaimer modal to appear and then click Continue.\n    # The modal has class .alertPopUp; the Continue input is inside it.\n    # Set up download + response listeners BEFORE clicking.\n    download_task = asyncio.create_task(page.context.wait_for_event(\"download\", timeout=90_000))\n    captured_csv: list[bytes] = []\n    captured_url: list[str] = []\n\n    async def on_response(response):\n        try:\n            ct = (response.headers.get(\"content-type\") or \"\").lower()\n            url = response.url.lower()\n            if (\n                \"text/csv\" in ct\n                or \"application/csv\" in ct\n                or url.endswith(\".csv\")\n                or \"downloadstatements\" in url\n                or \"midata\" in url\n            ):\n                if not captured_csv:\n                    try:\n                        body = await response.body()\n                        if body and len(body) > 50:\n                            captured_csv.append(body)\n                            captured_url.append(response.url)\n                            print(f\"  caught csv response: {response.url[:120]} ({len(body)} bytes)\")\n                    except Exception as e:\n                        print(f\"  response.body() failed: {e}\")\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n\n    page.context.on(\"response\", on_response)\n\n    # Click Continue — try native locator, then JS fallback.\n    clicked_continue = False\n    for sel in (\n        '.alertPopUp input[type=\"submit\"][value=\"Continue\"]',\n        'input[type=\"submit\"][value=\"Continue\"][name*=\"events.0\"]',\n        '.alertPopUp .primary',\n    ):\n        try:\n            loc = page.locator(sel).first\n            await loc.wait_for(state=\"visible\", timeout=8_000)\n            await loc.click(force=True, timeout=3_000)\n            print(f\"  clicked Continue via {sel}\")\n            clicked_continue = True\n            break\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  {sel} failed: {e}\")\n\n    if not clicked_continue:\n        try:\n            res = await page.evaluate(\"\"\"() => {\n                const inputs = [...document.querySelectorAll('input[type=\"submit\"]')];\n                const cont = inputs.find(i => (i.value || '').trim() === 'Continue');\n                if (cont) { cont.click(); return 'js-click'; }\n                return null;\n            }\"\"\")\n            if res:\n                print(f\"  clicked Continue via JS\")\n                clicked_continue = True\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  JS Continue click error: {e}\")\n\n    if not clicked_continue:\n        page.context.remove_listener(\"response\", on_response)\n        download_task.cancel()\n        await common.dump_state(page, OUTPUT_DIR, stamp, \"no_continue_button\")\n        raise RuntimeError(\"could not click Continue on disclaimer modal — see dump\")\n\n    # 'input[name=\"password\"]',\n    'input[type=\"password\"]',\n    'input[autocomplete=\"current-password\"]',\n]\nTOTP_INPUT_SELECTORS = [\n    'input[name=\"code\"]',\n    'input[autocomplete=\"one-time-code\"]',\n    'input[inputmode=\"numeric\"][maxlength=\"6\"]',\n    'input[type=\"text\"][maxlength=\"6\"]',\n]\n\n\ndef _looks_logged_in(url: str) -> bool:\n    lower = url.lower()\n    if any(x in lower for x in (\"login\", \"signin\", \"sign-in\", \"otp\", \"verify\", \"challenge\")):\n        return False\n    return \"trading212.com\" in lower and (\"dashboard\" in lower or lower.rstrip(\"/\").endswith(\"trading212.com\"))\n\n\nasync def run(headed: bool) -> int:\n    stamp = common.now_stamp()\n\n    async with async_playwright() as p:\n        ctx = await p.chromium.launch_persistent_context(\n            user_data_dir=str(PROFILE_DIR),\n            headless=not headed,\n            accept_downloads=True,\n            viewport={\"width\": 1400, \"height\": 900},\n        )\n        for existing in list(ctx.pages):\n            try:\n                await existing.close()\n            except Exception:\n                pass\n        page = await ctx.new_page()\n\n        try:\n            await page.goto(APP_URL, wait_until=\"domcontentloaded\", timeout=30_000)\n        except PlaywrightTimeout:\n            print(\"Initial navigation timed out.\")\n            return 1\n\n        try:\n            await page.wait_for_load_state(\"networkidle\", timeout=15_000)\n        except PlaywrightTimeout:\n            pass\n\n        await common.dismiss_cookie_banner(page)\n\n        if not _looks_logged_in(page.url):\n            await interactive_login(page, stamp)\n            timeout = 600_000 if headed else 30_000\n            try:\n                await page.wait_for_url(_looks_logged_in, timeout=timeout)\n            except PlaywrightTimeout:\n                await common.dump_state(page, OUTPUT_DIR, stamp, \"post_login_stuck\")\n                print(f\"Didn't reach dashboard. Final URL: {page.url}\")\n                return 3\n\n        await page.wait_for_load_state(\"networkidle\", timeout=30_000)\n        print(f\"Landed on: {page.url}\")\n\n        # Try each account in turn; failures dump state but don't abort the run.\n        for account in ACCOUNTS:\n            try:\n                await switch_account(page, account, stamp)\n                await download_account_csv(page, account, stamp)\n            except Exception as e:\n                await common.dump_state(page, OUTPUT_DIR, stamp, f\"{account}_failed\")\n                print(f\"  {account} failed: {e}\")\n\n        await ctx.close()\n        return 0\n\n\nasync def interactive_login(page, stamp: str) -> None:\n    username, password = get_credentials(PROVIDER)\n    if not (username and password):\n        print(\"No credentials resolved — fill manually.\")\n        return\n\n    print(\"Filling credentials...\")\n    if not await common.first_visible_fill(page, EMAIL_SELECTORS, username, \"email\"):\n        await common.dump_state(page, OUTPUT_DIR, stamp, \"no_email_field\")\n        print(\"  could not find email field\")\n        return\n\n    if not await common.first_visible_fill(page, PASSWORD_SELECTORS, password, \"password\"):\n        await common.dump_state(page, OUTPUT_DIR, stamp, \"no_password_field\")\n        print(\"  could not find password field\")\n        return\n\n    await common.tick_remember_me(page)\n\n    if not await common.click_login_button(page):\n        await common.dump_state(page, OUTPUT_DIR, stamp, \"no_login_button\")\n        print(\"  could not click login button\")\n        return\n    print(\"  submitted login\")\n\n    # Wait for the TOTP screen and auto-fill from Bitwarden.\n    await page.wait_for_timeout(2000)\n    await fill_totp_if_present(page, stamp)\n\n\nasync def fill_totp_if_present(page, stamp: str) -> None:\n    # Detect the TOTP input.\n    totp_input = None\n    for sel in TOTP_INPUT_SELECTORS:\n        try:\n            loc = page.locator(sel).first\n            if await loc.is_visible(timeout=2000):\n                totp_input = loc\n                print(f\"  detected TOTP input: {sel}\")\n                break\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n\n    if totp_input is None:\n        # Maybe there are 6 individual digit boxes.\n        try:\n            inputs = await page.locator('input[maxlength=\"1\"]').all()\n            if len(inputs) == 6:\n                code = get_totp(PROVIDER)\n                if not code:\n                    print(\"  no TOTP from Bitwarden — fill manually\")\n                    return\n                await inputs[0].click()\n                await page.keyboard.type(code, delay=80)\n                print(f\"  filled 6-digit TOTP\")\n                return\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n        print(\"  no TOTP prompt visible — assuming session is trusted\")\n        return\n\n    code = get_totp(PROVIDER)\n    if not code:\n        print(\"  no TOTP code from Bitwarden (item missing TOTP secret?) — fill manually\")\n        return\n\n    await common.type_into(totp_input, code)\n    print(f\"  filled TOTP code\")\n    # Submit — usually auto-advances, but try Enter as fallback.\n    try:\n        await page.keyboard.press(\"Enter\")\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n\n\nasync def switch_account(page, account: str, stamp: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Switch to the named account (invest / cash_isa) via T212's account\n    selector. Best-effort — dumps state on failure.\"\"\"\n    print(f\"Switching to {account}...\")\n    label_candidates = {\n        \"invest\": (\"Invest\", \"Stocks ISA\", \"ISA\"),\n        \"cash_isa\": (\"Cash ISA\", \"Savings\"),\n    }\n    candidates = label_candidates.get(account, ())\n\n    # Click the account-switcher (typically a sidebar or top-right control).\n    opened = await common.first_visible_click(\n        page,\n        [\n            '[data-qa-account-switcher]',\n            '[data-testid*=\"account-switcher\" i]',\n            'button[aria-label*=\"account\" i]',\n            'div[class*=\"AccountSwitcher\" i]',\n        ],\n        \"account switcher\",\n    )\n    if opened:\n        await page.wait_for_timeout(800)\n\n    for label in candidates:\n        try:\n            el = page.get_by_text(label, exact=False).first\n            if await el.is_visible(timeout=1000):\n                await el.click(force=True)\n                print(f\"  selected '{label}'\")\n                await page.wait_for_load_state(\"networkidle\", timeout=20_000)\n                return\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n\n    raise RuntimeError(f\"could not switch to {account} (tried: {candidates})\")\n\n\nasync def download_account_csv(page, account: str, stamp: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Open the History/Activity section for the current account and\n    download a CSV export.\"\"\"\n    print(f\"Downloading {account} CSV...\")\n\n    # Navigate to history/activity.\n    clicked = await common.first_visible_click(\n        page,\n        [\n            'a:has-text(\"History\")',\n            'button:has-text(\"History\")',\n            'a:has-text(\"Activity\")',\n            'a:has-text(\"Statements\")',\n            '[data-qa*=\"history\" i]',\n        ],\n        \"history/activity\",\n    )\n    if not clicked:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"could not find History/Activity link\")\n    await page.wait_for_load_state(\"networkidle\", timeout=20_000)\n    await page.wait_for_timeout(800)\n\n    # Open the export dialog.\n    clicked = await common.first_visible_click(\n        page,\n        [\n            'button:has-text(\"Export\")',\n            'a:has-text(\"Export\")',\n            'button:has-text(\"Download\")',\n            'button[aria-label*=\"export\" i]',\n        ],\n        \"Export button\",\n    )\n    if not clicked:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"could not find Export button\")\n\n    await page.wait_for_timeout(1200)\n\n    # Try to pick CSV if there's a format selector.\n    for sel in ('input[value=\"csv\" i]', 'label:has-text(\"CSV\")', 'button:has-text(\"CSV\")'):\n        try:\n            loc = page.locator(sel).first\n            if await loc.is_visible(timeout=500):\n                await loc.click(force=True)\n                print(\"  selected CSV format\")\n                break\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n\n    # Confirm / download.\n    async with page.expect_download(timeout=60_000) as dl_info:\n        clicked = await common.first_visible_click(\n            page,\n            [\n                'button:has-text(\"Download\")',\n                'button:has-text(\"Export\")',\n                'button:has-text(\"Confirm\")',\n                'input[type=\"submit\"][value*=\"Download\" i]',\n            ],\n            \"Confirm download button\",\n        )\n        if not clicked:\n            raise RuntimeError(\"could not click download confirm\")\n    download = await dl_info.value\n    suggested = download.suggested_filename or f\"trading212_{account}.csv\"\n    path = OUTPUT_DIR / f\"{common.now_stamp()}_{account}_{suggested}\"\n    await download.save_as(str(path))\n    size = path.stat().st_size\n    print(f\"  downloaded {account} ({size} bytes): {path}\")\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--headed\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"Show the browser window.\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    return asyncio.run(run(headed=common.auto_headed(PROFILE_DIR, args.headed)))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n"

+def get_totp(provider: str) -> str | None:
+    """Return the current 6-digit TOTP code for a provider's BW item.
+    Requires the item to have a TOTP secret configured in its Login section."""
+    session = os.environ.get("BW_SESSION")
+    if not session:
+        return None
+    item_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider.upper()}_BW_ITEM", provider)
+    try:
+        result = subprocess.run(
+            ["bw", "get", "totp", item_name, "--session", session],
+            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15,
+        )
+    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
+        return None
+    if result.returncode != 0:
+        return None
+    code = result.stdout.strip()
+    return code if code.isdigit() and len(code) == 6 else None

  "content": "\"\"\"\nRun every bank scraper in sequence.\n\nDesigned for monthly hands-off runs. You'll still need to handle the\nhuman-in-the-loop bits (Nationwide SMS code, Santander OTP, Revolut push\nnotification), but everything else proceeds automatically. Each provider\nruns in its own subprocess so one provider's crash can't take down the\nothers.\n\nUsage:\n    python -m scrapers.run_all                # all providers, headed\n    python -m scrapers.run_all --only amex,revolut\n    python -m scrapers.run_all --headless     # only useful for trusted sessions\n\nSet BW_SESSION first (use a session from `bw login`, not `bw unlock` — see\ncreds.py for why):\n    export BW_SESSION=\"$(bw login --raw 2>/dev/null || bw unlock --raw)\"\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nPROVIDERS = (\"amex\", \"barclaycard\", \"nationwide\", \"revolut\", \"santander\")\n\n\ndef run_one(provider: str, headed: bool) -> tuple[bool, float]:\n    cmd = [sys.executable, \"-m\", f\"scrapers.{provider}\"]\n    if headed:\n        cmd.append(\"--headed\")\n    print(f\"\\n{'='*60}\\n  {provider.upper()}\\n{'='*60}\")\n    start = time.monotonic()\n    result = subprocess.run(cmd, env=os.environ.copy())\n    elapsed = time.monotonic() - start\n    return result.returncode == 0, elapsed\n\n\ndef latest_output(provider: str) -> Path | None:\n    out_dir = Path.home() / \".argus\" / \"finance\" / \"raw\" / provider\n    if not out_dir.exists():\n        return None\n    candidates = [\n        p for p in out_dir.iterdir()\n        if p.is_file()\n        and p.suffix.lower() in (\".csv\", \".xlsx\", \".pdf\", \".xls\")\n        and not p.name.startswith(\".\")\n    ]\n    if not candidates:\n        return None\n    return max(candidates, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--only\", help=\"Comma-separated subset (e.g. amex,revolut)\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--headless\", action=\"store_true\",\n                        help=\"Run all scrapers headless — only works if every session is trusted\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n\n    if not os.environ.get(\"BW_SESSION\"):\n        print(\"BW_SESSION is not set — credentials will only resolve from \"\n              \"~/.argus/bw_cache/ if you've cached them there.\")\n\n    providers = PROVIDERS\n    if args.only:\n        wanted = {p.strip().lower() for p in args.only.split(\",\") if p.strip()}\n        unknown = wanted - set(PROVIDERS)\n        if unknown:\n            print(f\"Unknown providers: {sorted(unknown)} (valid: {PROVIDERS})\")\n            return 2\n        providers = tuple(p for p in PROVIDERS if p in wanted)\n\n    print(f\"Running {len(providers)} scraper(s): {', '.join(providers)}\")\n    results: list[tuple[str, bool, float, Path | None]] = []\n    for provider in providers:\n        before = latest_output(provider)\n        before_mtime = before.stat().st_mtime if before else 0\n        ok, elapsed = run_one(provider, headed=not args.headless)\n        after = latest_output(provider)\n        # Treat as success only if a new file landed since we started.\n        downloaded_new = bool(after and after.stat().st_mtime > before_mtime)\n        results.append((provider, ok and downloaded_new, elapsed, after if downloaded_new else None))\n\n    print(f\"\\n{'='*60}\\n  SUMMARY\\n{'='*60}\")\n    for provider, ok, elapsed, path in results:\n        mark = \"✓\" if ok else \"✗\"\n        path_str = f\" → {path.name}\" if path else \"\"\n        print(f\"  {mark} {provider:<13} {elapsed:>6.1f}s{path_str}\")\n\n    failures = [p for p, ok, *_ in results if not ok]\n    return 0 if not failures else 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n"
}

Try it:

```

```

Each provider runs in its own subprocess so one crashing won't kill the others. Order is alphabetical (`amex → barclaycard → nationwide → revolut → santander`) — Nationwide will pause for your SMS, Santander for OTP, Revolut for the push approval, the others should fly through if device-trust is intact.

End-of-run summary shows `✓` only if a fresh file actually landed on disk (mtime newer than when the run started) — so a script that "succeeds" but doesn't download anything still shows as `✗`.

> AGENT

Updated:
- **Revolut** now handles the "Statement is ready → click Download" alternative path
- **`run_all.py`** default is `--headed nationwide` so only Nationwide opens a window for SMS OTP, everything else runs headless

For your server question — two realistic options:

**Option 1 (simplest): Just run it on your Mac monthly.**
```
python -m scrapers.run_all
```
Nationwide opens a window for SMS, the other 4 run headless behind it. Takes ~2 minutes of attention once a month. No VPS deployment needed.

**Option 2: VPS unattended (everything except Nationwide).**
Copy your trusted-session profile dirs over once:
```
rsync -a ~/.argus/finance/profiles/{amex,barclaycard,revolut,santander}/ argus:~/.argus/finance/profiles/<provider>/
```
Then on the VPS, cron monthly:
```
0 9 1 * * BW_SESSION=... python -m scrapers.run_all --only amex,barclaycard,revolut,santander --headed none
```
You still do Nationwide manually on the Mac.

I'd start with Option 1 — it's much less moving parts. If a month of that gets tedious you can promote to Option 2.

"""Fitness database — SQLite storage for workouts, measurements, and stats."""

import json

import sqlite3

from .config import ARGUS_HOME, log

    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(DB_PATH))
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    return conn

DB initialised at `~/.argus/finance/finance.db`. Three tables:

- **`transactions`** — the core. Captures every field any provider gives (date, completed_date, amount, fee, balance_after, description, merchant, transaction_type, counterparty, reference, provider_category) plus enrichment fields (our `category`/`subcategory`/`tags`/`notes`/`is_transfer`/`paired_transaction_id`) and the full `raw_json` of the original row. `dedup_hash` is UNIQUE so re-importing the same CSV is a no-op.

- **`imports`** — one row per file ingested. Tracks what landed, when, and any errors.

- **`category_rules`** — for the categorisation step later (substring/regex/exact rules against description/merchant).

> AGENT

Let's go in groups, so we can pause and adjust. I'll start with **source/provenance** — the fields that say where a row came from.

```
provider         TEXT NOT NULL          -- 'amex', 'barclaycard', etc.
account          TEXT                   -- 'FlexDirect ****44568' / 'Revolut Current'
source_file      TEXT NOT NULL          -- path of CSV/PDF this row came from
imported_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
dedup_hash       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE   -- prevents double-import
```

**Decisions worth questioning:**

- **`account`** — nullable text. Some providers give you a clear account label (Nationwide: `"FlexDirect Account ****44568"`), others don't really (Barclaycard CSV has just card payments, no account label). Card-only providers we might leave NULL or fill with `"amex"` / `"barclaycard"`. Alternative: lift accounts into a separate `accounts` table now, FK by id — cleaner if you ever hold multiple cards or accounts per provider.

- **`source_file`** — full path. Useful for re-ingest / debugging. The path includes the timestamp prefix so it's stable. Could be relative-to-`~/.argus/finance/raw` instead, to survive moves.

- **`dedup_hash`** — needs to be deterministic across re-imports. I was planning `sha256(provider | account | date | amount | description)`. But Amex has a stable `Reference` field — for Amex specifically we should use that as the dedup key. For Revolut, the `Completed Date` is more stable than `Started Date`. Worth thinking about per-provider.

- **No `account_currency`** — I assumed everything's GBP. Revolut multi-currency could break that (you have foreign-currency transactions). Add a per-account currency, or trust the per-row `currency` field, or assume GBP only?

Thoughts on these four before I move to the dates section?

okay tha'sts good but I wna tsomehting on there to show credit or debit

> AGENT

Good call. Two ways to do it:

**Option A — explicit `direction` column, generated from amount:**
```sql
amount    REAL NOT NULL                    -- signed: + = into account, - = out
direction TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
              CASE WHEN amount >= 0 THEN 'credit' ELSE 'debit' END
          ) STORED
```
SQLite computes it on insert, you can index it, can't drift out of sync.

**Option B — separate `paid_in` / `paid_out` columns** (the Nationwide CSV style):
```sql
paid_in   REAL                             -- NULL or amount in
paid_out  REAL                             -- NULL or amount out
```
Closer to how banks present statements, but most queries become `COALESCE(paid_in, 0) - COALESCE(paid_out, 0)` and aggregations are annoying. Recommend against unless you really like seeing the columns side-by-side.

I'd go A. **But there's a deeper question:** sign convention for **credit cards**.

- **Bank accounts** (Nationwide, Revolut, Santander): salary in = `+`, spending = `-`. Easy.
- **Credit cards** (Amex, Barclaycard): in their CSV, a *purchase* is a positive number (Barclaycard `16.10` for an eBay buy). A *payment to clear the card* is negative (`-359.17`). That's because they're showing "amount you owe goes up".

For our unified table I'd flip the credit-card signs at ingest so the convention is consistent: **`+` always means money flowed INTO the account, `-` means OUT**. A card purchase becomes `-16.10` (money left the card account, your debt went up). A payment becomes `+359.17` (money came in, debt went down).

OK with both — generated `direction` column, and flipping credit-card signs at ingest?

Got it — that's the account *type*, not transaction direction. So:

```
account_type   TEXT NOT NULL    -- 'credit_card' for Amex + Barclaycard
                                -- 'debit'       for Nationwide + Santander + Revolut
```

(Could later add `'savings'`, `'isa'`, `'investment'` if you bring T212/HL in.)

Two questions:

1. **Store it per-transaction (denormalised)** or **derive it at query time from provider** (since every Amex row = `credit_card`, every Nationwide row = `debit`)? Per-transaction is simpler to query but redundant; deriving keeps the table clean but every report needs the lookup. I'd say per-transaction — disk is cheap, joins are friction.

2. Should I keep `direction` (credit/debit transaction flow) as well, or is `account_type` enough for now? They're orthogonal: a Barclaycard *purchase* and an Amex *refund* are both `credit_card` account, but one's a debit-direction and one's a credit-direction transaction.

> DEVELOPER

idkw hat do you think is best

> AGENT

My take:

- **Drop `direction` entirely.** It's literally just `amount >= 0`. Inlining `WHERE amount < 0` in queries is fine; adding a generated column for it is gold-plating.
- **Keep `account_type` as a per-row column.** Tiny denormalisation, makes "show me credit-card spend vs debit spend" a one-liner with no joins. Worth the redundancy.

So:
```
account_type   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (account_type IN ('credit_card','debit'))
amount         REAL NOT NULL    -- + = into account, - = out (credit-card signs flipped at ingest)
```

We can expand the CHECK constraint to `'savings','isa','investment'` if/when those providers come online — easy migration.

> AGENT

Two ways to go:

**Option 1 — `providers` lookup table** (simpler):
```sql
CREATE TABLE providers (
    name           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,    -- 'amex', 'nationwide', etc.
    account_type   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (account_type IN ('credit_card','debit','savings','isa','investment')),
    display_name   TEXT                 -- 'American Express' for nicer reports
);
```
Transactions still have `provider TEXT`, joined to this for the type. One row per provider, seeded once.

**Option 2 — full `accounts` table** (more flexible):
```sql
CREATE TABLE accounts (
    id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    provider       TEXT NOT NULL,
    label          TEXT NOT NULL,       -- 'FlexDirect ****44568' or 'default'
    account_type   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (...),
    currency       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GBP',
    display_name   TEXT,
    active         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    UNIQUE(provider, label)
);
```
Transactions reference `account_id INTEGER REFERENCES accounts(id)`. Handles "two Nationwide accounts of different types" (FlexDirect = debit, ISA Savings = isa) cleanly.

**My recommendation: Option 2.** Today every provider is one type, but the moment T212 comes in (Stocks ISA + Cash ISA under the same login = two accounts, two types under one provider) the simpler model breaks. Also gives you a natural home for per-account currency (Revolut), display names, active/closed status, etc.

Cost: ingest has to upsert into `accounts` before inserting transactions. That's ~10 lines of code.

Go with Option 2?

| Nationwide | `Date` | `04 May 2026` |
| Revolut | `Started Date` + `Completed Date` | `2026-05-01 02:00:05` (both have time) |
| Santander | `Date` | `15/04/2026` |

Proposed:
```sql
date            TEXT NOT NULL    -- YYYY-MM-DD, primary "happened" date
completed_date  TEXT             -- YYYY-MM-DD, NULL when same as date or not given
```

**Decisions:**

1. **Normalise everything to ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`** at ingest. Sorts lexicographically, no ambiguity, parses cleanly. SQLite has no DATE type — TEXT is the idiomatic choice.

2. **Drop the time component** even for Revolut. Sub-day ordering is rarely interesting for budgeting, and the full timestamp lives in `raw_json` if you ever want it. If you'd rather keep it, we can add a `time TEXT` column or store full ISO datetime.

3. **`completed_date`** — only Revolut splits these. For others, leave NULL (same as `date`). For Revolut, populate both. Sort/aggregate queries default to `date`.

4. **Which is "the date" for Revolut** — `Started Date` or `Completed Date`? I'd use **Completed** as the primary `date` since that's when money actually moved and matches what your bank balance reflects. `Started Date` goes into `completed_date`... wait that's backwards. Let me think.

Actually clearer naming would be:
```sql
date           TEXT NOT NULL    -- when money settled (primary, used for reports)
initiated_date TEXT             -- when the txn was started (Revolut splits this)
```

Settle date is what matters for "money in/out this month" reports. Started date is more of a curiosity.

Sound right?

Onto **money** fields.

```sql
amount          REAL NOT NULL              -- signed: + = into account, - = out (credit-card signs flipped at ingest)
currency        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GBP' -- of THIS transaction
fee             REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0    -- explicit fee (Revolut surfaces it as a column)
balance_after   REAL                       -- running balance after this txn, NULL for credit cards
```

**Decisions:**

1. **`currency` on the transaction even though we have it on `accounts`** — yes. Revolut lets you spend EUR from a GBP account; the transaction's currency can differ from the account's home currency. For now everything will be GBP, but the column is cheap to include and saves a migration later.

2. **`fee`** — only Revolut breaks this out (e.g. the Premium plan fee was shown as `0.00` amount + `7.99` fee). For others it's embedded in `description` or already netted into `amount`. Default 0.

3. **`balance_after`** — debit accounts (Nationwide/Revolut/Santander) all give running balances, credit cards (Amex/Barclaycard) don't. NULL for cards. Useful for sanity-checking parsers against bank reality.

**Optional: FX columns** for foreign-currency transactions:
```sql
fx_amount       REAL    -- original amount in original currency
fx_currency     TEXT    -- 'EUR', 'USD' etc.
fx_rate         REAL    -- rate applied
```
Most providers either bury this in the description or don't surface it at all. I'd **skip these for v1** — the info's in `raw_json` if you ever need it, and adding columns later is cheap.

> AGENT

Yes, this is a separate concept and worth a dedicated table. Let me lay out the options:

**Concept 1: `balance_snapshots` table** — generic balance snapshots over time, for both debit and credit accounts:
```sql
CREATE TABLE balance_snapshots (
    id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    account_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    date         TEXT NOT NULL,         -- YYYY-MM-DD
    balance      REAL NOT NULL,         -- for credit cards: + = amount owed
    source       TEXT NOT NULL,         -- 'manual', 'statement', 'scraper', 'dashboard'
    notes        TEXT,
    UNIQUE(account_id, date, source)
);
```
- For debit accounts: balance of money in the account.
- For credit cards: amount currently owed (the "bill to pay off").
- Populated however: you type it in via Telegram, or a future scraper grabs it from the dashboard, or you read it off a statement PDF.
- "Current bill" = `SELECT balance FROM balance_snapshots WHERE account_id=? ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 1`.

**Concept 2: also add `statements` table** for credit-card statements specifically:
```sql
CREATE TABLE statements (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    account_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    statement_date  TEXT NOT NULL,     -- when the statement was issued
    period_start    TEXT NOT NULL,
    period_end      TEXT NOT NULL,
    closing_balance REAL NOT NULL,     -- what you must pay
    minimum_payment REAL,
    due_date        TEXT,
    paid            INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    UNIQUE(account_id, statement_date)
);
```
- Captures statement-level info: "you owe £487 by 15 June, minimum £25".
- More granular than snapshots — tracks the billing cycle.

**My take:** Start with **just `balance_snapshots`** — covers your "what's the bill to pay off?" question simply. `statements` is a layer on top that needs PDF parsing or dashboard scraping to populate; we don't have that yet. Add it later if/when we want due-date reminders.

Snapshots good for now, or do you want statements too?

but do we have to calculate the balance ourselves or what?

> AGENT

Good question — depends on the account type. Three sources, in order of accuracy:

**For debit accounts (Nationwide / Revolut / Santander):**
- The CSV gives `balance_after` per row → we already store this on every transaction.
- "Current balance" = `balance_after` of the latest transaction → trivial query, no separate table strictly needed.

**For credit cards (Amex / Barclaycard):**
- CSV has only transactions, **no balance**. Three ways to populate:

  1. **Compute it** — cumulative sum of all credit-card transactions since you started. Drifts over time if we miss any (statement fees we didn't capture, interest, etc.). Useless without an anchor.
  
  2. **Scrape it from the dashboard** — both Amex and Barclaycard show "current balance" prominently after login. Extend the scrapers to grab that number once per run and write a row into `balance_snapshots`. **Most reliable, fully automated, ~10 lines per scraper.**
  
  3. **Manual entry** — Telegram command like `/balance amex 487.23`. Fine as a fallback, annoying as a primary.

**My recommendation:**
- For credit cards: scrape the dashboard balance during the existing scraper run. We're already authenticated and on the right page anyway.
- For debit accounts: just use the latest transaction's `balance_after`. No snapshots table needed unless you want historical points (e.g. for plotting net worth over time).

So the design we land on for balances:

```sql
CREATE TABLE balance_snapshots (
    id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    account_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    date         TEXT NOT NULL,         -- YYYY-MM-DD
    balance      REAL NOT NULL,         -- credit cards: + = currently owed

);
```

- Credit card scrapers (Amex, Barclaycard) get extended to scrape the visible balance from the dashboard once per run, write a row in `balance_snapshots`. "What do I owe right now?" = `SELECT balance FROM balance_snapshots WHERE account_id=X ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 1`.
- Debit accounts: no snapshot table needed for "current balance" (latest transaction's `balance_after` covers it), but we *could* write snapshots too if you want historical net-worth plotting later.
- No `statements` table — you pay in full, so no due-date / minimum-payment modelling needed.

> AGENT

Translating their reply:
- **Sandbox docs** = fake test data, not your actual accounts. Useless for real finance tracking.
- **Core Exchange** = for businesses that *provide* data to Plaid (banks/FIs), not consume it.
- **"Book a meeting"** = sales conversation about a paid commercial plan.

What he's *not* mentioning (because they'd rather you book the call): Plaid has a **free Development tier** — 100 Items, real production data, no commercial agreement needed. That's the actual fit for personal use. You sign up at dashboard.plaid.com, get API keys, build against it.

UK coverage via Open Banking covers Nationwide, Santander, Revolut, Barclays — but **Amex isn't supported** in UK, and Plaid's BCC/Barclaycard coverage is hit-and-miss.

**My read: don't pivot.** Your scrapers cover all 5 providers including Amex. Plaid would replace at most 3-4 of them, you'd still need scrapers for the rest, and you'd add a quarterly re-consent flow (Open Banking sessions expire every 90 days). The reliability win is real but the architecture gets messier, not simpler.

Worth exploring if Nationwide SMS becomes a recurring pain. Until then, the scrapers are working — keep going on the schema.

> AGENT

Yes — Playwright has proper "wait for content" primitives. The pattern is:

- **`await element.wait_for(state="visible")`** — wait for the specific element you're about to click. Returns as soon as it's there.
- **`await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")`** — wait for HTTP traffic to settle.
- **`await page.wait_for_url(predicate)`** — wait for a navigation.

`wait_for_timeout` is the lazy fallback — it sleeps a fixed amount whether or not it's needed. Most of mine are leftovers from "this worked, ship it" iterations.

Let me sweep the biggest offenders (Santander has 8 of them, Nationwide and Revolut a few each):

306	async def download_midata(page, stamp: str) -> None:
307	    # View transactions on the main account tile.
308	    clicked = await common.first_visible_click(
309	        page,
310	        [
311	            'a:has-text("View transactions")',
312	            'button:has-text("View transactions")',
313	            'a:has-text("View account")',
314	            'a[href*="transactions" i]',
315	        ],
316	        "View transactions",
317	    )
318	    if not clicked:
319	        raise RuntimeError("could not find 'View transactions' link")
320	    await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle", timeout=20_000)
321	    await page.wait_for_timeout(800)
322	
323	    # Open the Download Transactions page.
324	    clicked = await common.first_visible_click(
325	        page,
326	        [
327	            'a:has-text("Download transactions")',
328	            'button:has-text("Download transactions")',
329	            'a[href*="download" i]',
330	        ],
331	        "Download transactions",
332	    )
333	    if not clicked:
334	        raise RuntimeError("could not find 'Download transactions' link")
335	    await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle", timeout=20_000)
336	    await page.wait_for_timeout(800)
337	
338	    # Pick Midata from the format dropdown — 12 months CSV, no date entry.
339	    # value="6" is the Midata (csv) option; safer than label matching.
340	    picked = False
341	    for sel in ("#sel_downloadto", 'select[name="downloadStatementsForm.typeFile"]', "select"):
342	        try:
343	            dropdown = page.locator(sel).first
344	            if await dropdown.is_visible(timeout=1500):
345	                try:
346	                    await dropdown.select_option(value="6")
347	                except Exception:
348	                    await dropdown.select_option(label="Midata (csv)")
349	                print("  selected Midata (csv)")
350	                picked = True
351	                break
352	        except Exception:
353	            continue
354	
355	    if not picked:
356	        await common.dump_state(page, OUTPUT_DIR, stamp, "no_format_dropdown")
357	        raise RuntimeError("could not find format dropdown — see dump")
358	
359	    # Dropdown has submitonchange — page navigates to a midata disclaimer.
360	    try:
361	        await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle", timeout=15_000)
362	    except PlaywrightTimeout:
363	        pass
364	    await page.wait_for_timeout(800)
365	    await dismiss_inactivity_modal(page)
366	
367	    # Click Download (#alertConfirm) to open the disclaimer modal, then
368	    # click Continue inside the modal. The Continue click triggers the
369	    # actual CSV download — wrap it in expect_download so Playwright
370	    # intercepts it cleanly (don't touch response.body — that interferes
371	    # with Chromium's attachment handling and corrupts the file).
372	    try:
373	        dl = page.locator("#alertConfirm").first
374	        await dl.wait_for(state="visible", timeout=8_000)
375	        await dl.click(force=True, timeout=3_000)
376	        print("  clicked Download (#alertConfirm)")
377	    except Exception as e:
378	        await common.dump_state(page, OUTPUT_DIR, stamp, "no_download_button")
379	        raise RuntimeError(f"could not click Download: {e}")
380	
381	    await page.wait_for_timeout(800)
382	    await dismiss_inactivity_modal(page)
383	
384	    # Wait for the modal's Continue to be clickable.

> AGENT

**Found it.** The dump's "Service Message" reads:

> "The form could not be submitted as the following fields have errors / Field top Level has error: invisible"

That's anti-bot detection — Barclaycard has an invisible field that JS populates, and that JS refuses to fill it when it detects headless Chromium. Same class of problem as Revolut and T212 had. Solution: add `playwright-stealth`.

> AGENT

A few options, in increasing complexity:

**1. Use real Chrome (not bundled Chromium)** — one-line change, often defeats fingerprinting.
```python
ctx = await p.chromium.launch_persistent_context(
    user_data_dir=str(PROFILE_DIR),
    channel="chrome",   # ← uses your installed Chrome stable
    ...
)
```
Real Chrome doesn't set `navigator.webdriver=true`, doesn't have the headless-Chromium fingerprint. Often enough.

**2. Mobile emulation** — emulate iPhone Safari. Banks usually allow mobile freely because their app users hit the same flow.

**3. Connect to your real running Chrome via CDP** — launch Chrome yourself with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`, Playwright connects to it. Real browser, real session, zero fingerprint diff. Adds setup friction.

**4. Give up and run headed** — what we know works.

Let me try option 1 first — cheapest, most likely to work:

Looking at the screenshot — the page now shows a **CVV step-up challenge with a red error** ("Please enter the correct 3-digit security code"), and **all our filled values appear empty in the rendered form**. This is React-controlled inputs rejecting scripted input — Barclaycard's anti-bot detects that the value changes don't come from trusted user events.

This is a tougher class of detection than stealth or Brave can fix. The pragmatic answer is what worked: **run Barclaycard headed**. It's annoying but a real Chromium window in foreground generates trusted events.

> AGENT

Honestly, there are more avenues — I was suggesting we accept the cheapest fix. Let me list what we haven't tried, in order of effort:

**1. Mobile emulation (cheapest)** — change viewport + user agent to iPhone Safari. Banks often serve a simpler mobile flow with less aggressive anti-bot. ~5 lines of code, may just work.

**2. Off-screen headed window** — open a real headed browser but at coordinates like `(-2000, -2000)` so it's invisible. Generates trusted events, doesn't interrupt you visually. macOS may refuse to fully hide it, but worth a try.

**3. `headless="new"` Chromium mode** — Playwright's modern headless (post-2022) uses the same renderer as headed and is much harder to fingerprint than legacy headless. May already be default but worth pinning explicitly.

**4. CDP-connect to a manually-launched Brave** — you (or a script) launches Brave once with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`, Playwright then `connect_over_cdp()`s into it. The browser is real, runs in the background, persists session across runs. Highest reliability, but setup adds a step.

**5. Use PSD2 Open Banking API for Barclays** — Barclays *does* expose Open Banking. Would need to OAuth-consent every 90 days, but no scraping at all after that. Largest pivot.

My recommendation order: try **1 (mobile) → 3 (headless=new) → 2 (off-screen) → 4 (CDP)** before settling for headed. Want me to try mobile emulation first? Cheapest swing.

1	"""
2	Run every bank scraper in sequence.
3	
4	Designed for monthly hands-off runs. You'll still need to handle the
5	human-in-the-loop bits (Nationwide SMS code, Santander OTP, Revolut push
6	notification), but everything else proceeds automatically. Each provider
7	runs in its own subprocess so one provider's crash can't take down the
8	others.
9	
10	Usage:
11	    python -m scrapers.run_all                       # all headless except those in --headed
12	    python -m scrapers.run_all --only amex,revolut
13	    python -m scrapers.run_all --headed nationwide   # only nationwide opens a window
14	    python -m scrapers.run_all --headed all          # legacy: open a window for every provider
15	
16	Server / VPS use: keep --headed providers minimal. Nationwide needs SMS OTP
17	each login → it can only run on a machine where you can see the browser
18	and type the code. The others have trusted-device sessions after first
19	login and can run unattended.
20	
21	Set BW_SESSION first (use a session from `bw login`, not `bw unlock` — see
22	creds.py for why).
23	"""
24	
25	import argparse
26	import os
27	import subprocess
28	import sys
29	import time
30	from pathlib import Path
31	
32	PROVIDERS = ("amex", "barclaycard", "nationwide", "revolut", "santander")
33	
34	
35	def run_one(provider: str, headed: bool) -> tuple[bool, float]:
36	    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", f"scrapers.{provider}"]
37	    if headed:
38	        cmd.append("--headed")
39	    print(f"\n{'='*60}\n  {provider.upper()}\n{'='*60}")
40	    start = time.monotonic()
41	    result = subprocess.run(cmd, env=os.environ.copy())
42	    elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
43	    return result.returncode == 0, elapsed
44	
45	
46	def latest_output(provider: str) -> Path | None:
47	    out_dir = Path.home() / ".argus" / "finance" / "raw" / provider
48	    if not out_dir.exists():
49	        return None
50	    candidates = [
51	        p for p in out_dir.iterdir()
52	        if p.is_file()
53	        and p.suffix.lower() in (".csv", ".xlsx", ".pdf", ".xls")
54	        and not p.name.startswith(".")
55	    ]
56	    if not candidates:
57	        return None
58	    return max(candidates, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
59	
60	
61	def main() -> int:
62	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
63	    parser.add_argument("--only", help="Comma-separated subset (e.g. amex,revolut)")
64	    parser.add_argument("--headed", default="barclaycard,revolut",
65	                        help='Comma-separated providers to run headed; "all" or "none" also accepted (default: barclaycard,revolut)')
66	    args = parser.parse_args()
67	
68	    if not os.environ.get("BW_SESSION"):
69	        print("BW_SESSION is not set — credentials will only resolve from "
70	              "~/.argus/bw_cache/ if you've cached them there.")
71	
72	    providers = PROVIDERS
73	    if args.only:
74	        wanted = {p.strip().lower() for p in args.only.split(",") if p.strip()}
75	        unknown = wanted - set(PROVIDERS)
76	        if unknown:
77	            print(f"Unknown providers: {sorted(unknown)} (valid: {PROVIDERS})")
78	            return 2
79	        providers = tuple(p for p in PROVIDERS if p in wanted)
80	
81	    headed_arg = args.headed.strip().lower()
82	    if headed_arg == "all":
83	        headed_set = set(PROVIDERS)
84	    elif headed_arg in ("", "none"):
85	        headed_set = set()
86	    else:

Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. Let me compile my findings:

## Schema Design Conventions for finance_db

Based on reviewing `fitness_db.py`, `recipe_db.py`, and `db.py`, here are the shared conventions to replicate:

### **Database Setup Pattern**
- **DB location:** `ARGUS_HOME / "data" / {db_name}.db` (e.g., `/data/finance.db`)
- **get_db() pattern:**
  - `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` on DB_PATH.parent
  - `row_factory = sqlite3.Row` (enables dict-like access)
  - `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` (write-ahead logging for concurrency)
  - Return connection, caller closes
- **init_db() pattern:**
  - Use `executescript()` with multi-line CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
  - Handle migrations with try/except on `ALTER TABLE` (silent fail on duplicate columns)
  - Check `PRAGMA table_info()` when structural changes are complex
  - Call `conn.commit()` and `conn.close()` at end

### **Column Type Conventions**
- **Dates:** TEXT (ISO format `YYYY-MM-DD` or full datetime) — see fitness_db line 29 (`date TEXT NOT NULL`), query at fitness_web line 224
- **Booleans:** INTEGER (0/1) — see recipe_db line 42 (`freezable INTEGER DEFAULT 0`)
- **Decimals/Floats:** REAL (speeds, calories, reps) — see fitness_db line 36 (`distance REAL`)
- **Times:** INTEGER (seconds) — see fitness_db line 34 (`moving_time INTEGER`)
- **JSON blobs:** TEXT stored as `json.dumps()`, parsed with `json.loads()` — see recipe_db line 112, fitness_db line 119, 402

### **Relationships & Indexes**
- **Foreign Keys:** Use explicit REFERENCES in table definition — fitness_db line 28 (`activity_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES activities(id)`)
- **Unique Constraints:** Define at column level or composite — recipe_db line 29 (`name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`), fitness_db line 121 (`UNIQUE(activity_id, stream_type)`)
- **No explicit CREATE INDEX** (both dbs rely on table structure + FK + UNIQUE constraints)

### **Common Patterns to Mirror**
- **INSERT OR IGNORE/REPLACE:** Handle duplicates gracefully (recipe_db line 125, fitness_db line 261)
- **Timestamps:** Use `DEFAULT (datetime('now'))` in schema — recipe_db line 47, fitness_db line 140
- **created_at/completed_at:** Audit columns with `TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))` or manual updates — fitness_db lines 140-141
- **Seed functions:** Create `seed_*()` functions for reference data (fitness_db lines 762+)

### **Query Patterns for Transactions**
From fitness_web/app.py:
- **Date filtering:** String comparison works directly (`WHERE date DESC`) — line 69
- **Aggregation:** Use GROUP BY with JOINs for rolled-up views — line 73-75
- **Cascading deletes:** Manually delete related rows (no CASCADE) — lines 465-470
- **Bulk operations:** Single transaction, multiple inserts — fitness_db lines 624-640

### **Key Files to Reference**
- `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/argus/argus/src/fitness_db.py` — full schema + migration pattern
- `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/argus/argus/src/recipe_db.py` — simpler single-table example
- `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/argus/argus/src/db.py` — minimal base pattern (inline init)
- `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/argus/argus/fitness_web/app.py` — query examples (lines 66-78, 220-241)

### **Recommendations for finance_db**
1. **Mirror fitness_db structure exactly** — inline executescript, migrations with try/except
2. **Use TEXT for transaction dates**, INTEGER for amounts (as REAL if fractional cents matter, else multiply by 100 → INTEGER)
3. **Consider FK indexes on common filters:** account_id, transaction_type, date range queries
4. **Store raw bank response as JSON blob** if you want to preserve unmapped fields
5. **Keep cascading deletes manual** (no CASCADE) to avoid accidental purges
6. **Do NOT use separate .sql files** — keep executescript inline like fitness_db for portability

Like the split bills make sense but how would you know like 10 on bozze and 40 on groceries?

> AGENT

Fair point — the bank gives you one row: `SAINSBURYS £50`, not the line items. The only ways to know are:

1. **Manual entry** — you tap the transaction in some UI and split it `£40 groceries / £10 booze`. Annoying for most people; useful for people who really want pristine category reports.
2. **Receipt OCR** — scan the receipt, parse line items, attach to the transaction. Big build, separate project.
3. **Some providers' enhanced data** — Amex Detailed Activity occasionally gives line items, Plaid sometimes does. Inconsistent and rare.

Realistically for personal use, splits are over-engineered. The dominant pattern is: pick the dominant category (probably "Groceries") and move on. Over a year, the £10 booze "miscategorisations" average out and don't change the picture.

My honest recommendation: **skip splits in v1**. If you ever want them, you'd add a `transaction_splits` table later — it's a clean addition, no migration of existing rows needed.

Want me to go ahead with that recommendation? Or do any of the other three questions (hierarchical categories, multi-currency, recurring) need clarifying too?

## Goblin: Abandoned Personal Finance Planner - Exploration Report

**Architecture Summary:**
Goblin is a lightweight Streamlit-based budget tracker (no database—entirely CSV/JSON file-based). Last commit was March 2025. The project is intentionally minimal: a frontend dashboard pulling data from an external "Vulkan API" backend (not included in this repo).

**Data Model:**
- **Transaction schema** (CSV): Date, Name, Amount, Category, SubCategory, PaymentMethod, Notes. Flat two-level hierarchy (Category → SubCategory).
- **Budget model** (JSON): Simple key-value per month (2026-01 → {Groceries: £500, Transport: £200, ...}). 7 hardcoded categories: Groceries, Transport, Entertainment, Utilities, Healthcare, Shopping, Dining Out.
- **No primary database**—all data flows through Vulkan API (abstract, credentials in `.envrc`).

**Categorization Approach:**
Pure manual. Categories and subcategories are determined at transaction import time (upstream in Vulkan API). No rules engine, no LLM classification, no category mapping logic in this repo. The app filters out a hardcoded "Fun" category (line 40, `streamlit_budget.py`).

**Import/Ingest Flow:**
Black-boxed. VulkanAPI (`vulkan_api.py`) fetches CSV from `/vault/data` endpoint and budget JSON from `/vault/budget`. No parsers, deduplication, or reconciliation visible here. Data arrives pre-categorized. Test mode uses static CSVs for development.

**Notable Features Worth Borrowing:**
1. **Two-level category hierarchy** with subcategory rollups (e.g., Groceries → Weekly Shopping). Pivot-table aggregation on lines 59–90.
2. **Credit card tracking** (lines 256–275): Filters transactions by PaymentMethod, shows credit "pot" separately. Useful micro-feature.
3. **Month-to-month navigation** with session state (lines 139–162). Clean UX for exploring historical months.
4. **Dual mode** (API vs. test data): Elegant —— `--test` flag toggles between live and local CSVs. Good for development.
5. **Budget vs. actual comparison**: Remaining, overspend, percentage-used calculations (lines 87–105).

**Anti-Patterns / Dead Ends:**
1. **No database**: Everything in memory after CSV load. Scales poorly, no persistent notes/edits, no audit trail.
2. **Hardcoded budget categories**: New categories require code changes. Budget schema is fragile (assumes month string in YYYY-MM format).
3. **Vulkan API abstraction**: Core logic hidden upstream. This repo is just a thin UI wrapper—makes it hard to reason about categorization, dedup, or rule tuning without seeing the real backend.
4. **Incomplete income tab** (line 445–447): "Coming soon..." comment. Project abandoned before income was added.
5. **No error handling for missing data**: Falls back to warnings but UI still renders empty states ungracefully.

**Why Abandoned (Hints):**
- Last commit March 2025; no activity since. 
- README has generic setup docs but no troubleshooting or lessons learned.
- The Vulkan API is an external service—if that went down or credentials expired, the app becomes useless and painful to debug (no local fallback except test data).
- Likely hit a wall on categorization scalability or realized the abstraction (Vulkan) added more friction than value.

**Key Files:**
- `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/goblin/streamlit_budget.py` (620 lines): All dashboard logic, data transformations, UI.
- `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/goblin/vulkan_api.py` (33 lines): Thin API wrapper.
- `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/goblin/test/testbudget.json`: Budget fixture (7 categories, 2 months).
- `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/goblin/test/testout.csv`: Transaction fixture (~30 rows, realistic sample data).

## Approved Plan:
# Finance DB schema — unified transactions store

## Context

Five scrapers (Amex, Barclaycard, Nationwide, Revolut, Santander) now reliably download CSVs and balance JSON sidecars into `~/.argus/finance/raw/<provider>/`. The next step is parsing those into a single SQLite DB at `~/.argus/finance/finance.db` so we can answer questions like:

- "How much did I spend on Groceries last month?"
- "What do I owe on credit cards right now?"
- "Show me everything over £100 in May."
- "What's my net cashflow this year?"

The user's previous attempt (goblin, `/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/goblin/`) was a CSV-only Streamlit dashboard — useful conventions to borrow (hierarchical categories, credit-card pot view), but no DB persistence and reliant on an external API that became its own friction. This time we go SQLite-first.

User decisions made during design discussion:
- Account type lives on a separate `accounts` table (not denormalised on transactions) so we can have multiple accounts per provider with different types.
- Categories are hierarchical (parent_id), seeded with goblin's set.
- Multi-currency: keep `original_amount` + `original_currency` columns for Revolut foreign-currency txns.
- No splits in v1 (would need manual per-transaction split entry, rarely worth it).
- No recurring detection in v1 (`ALTER TABLE` later when needed).
- Credit card balances come from scraper JSON sidecars into `balance_snapshots`; debit account "current balance" uses latest transaction's `balance_after`.
- Credit card transaction signs are flipped at ingest so the convention is uniform: `+ = into account`, `- = out`.

## Schema design

DB location: `~/.argus/finance/finance.db` (next to raw files, outside the repo). Following the `fitness_db.py` pattern: single Python file `argus/src/finance_db.py` with `get_db()` + `init_db()` + `executescript()`. `journal_mode=WAL`, `row_factory=sqlite3.Row`, `foreign_keys=ON`.

### `accounts`
One row per (provider, account label). Auto-upserted at ingest based on what each parser extracts.

```sql
CREATE TABLE accounts (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    provider      TEXT NOT NULL,        -- 'amex' | 'barclaycard' | 'nationwide' | 'revolut' | 'santander'
    label         TEXT NOT NULL,        -- 'FlexDirect ****44568' | 'default'
    account_type  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (account_type IN
                    ('credit_card','debit','savings','isa','investment')),
    currency      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GBP',
    display_name  TEXT,
    institution   TEXT,                 -- 'Nationwide BS' (denorm, for nicer reports)
    active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    opened_at     TEXT,                 -- optional, manually entered
    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    UNIQUE(provider, label)
);
```

Seed with the five known accounts on `init_db()` (Amex + Barclaycard = credit_card, Nationwide + Santander + Revolut = debit).

### `categories`
Hierarchical via `parent_id`. Seeded with goblin's categories on init.

```sql
CREATE TABLE categories (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    parent_id     INTEGER REFERENCES categories(id),
    color         TEXT,                 -- hex, optional
    icon          TEXT,                 -- emoji, optional
    exclude_from_spending INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- 1 for 'Transfer'
    sort_order    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
```

Seed: `Food (> Groceries, Restaurants, Takeaway)`, `Transport (> Tube, Uber, Train, Car)`, `Entertainment`, `Utilities (> Internet, Phone, Energy)`, `Healthcare`, `Shopping (> Clothes, Electronics)`, `Subscriptions`, `Income (> Salary, Refund)`, `Transfer (exclude_from_spending=1)`, `Uncategorised`.

### `transactions`
The core. Lossless via `raw_json`. Dedup via `dedup_hash` UNIQUE.

```sql
CREATE TABLE transactions (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,

    -- Source / provenance
    account_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    source_file     TEXT NOT NULL,
    imported_at     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    dedup_hash      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,

    -- Time (YYYY-MM-DD; Revolut sub-day precision lives in raw_json)
    date            TEXT NOT NULL,        -- settle / posting date
    initiated_date  TEXT,                 -- only set when different (Revolut)

    -- Money (in account's home currency)
    amount          REAL NOT NULL,        -- signed: + = into account, - = out
    fee             REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    balance_after   REAL,                 -- NULL for credit cards

    -- Multi-currency (NULL when same as account currency)
    original_amount   REAL,
    original_currency TEXT,

    -- Descriptive
    description       TEXT NOT NULL,      -- raw, as the bank gave it
    merchant          TEXT,               -- cleaned (filled later)
    counterparty      TEXT,               -- 'To X' / 'From Y' for transfers
    transaction_type  TEXT,               -- provider's type label
    reference         TEXT,               -- provider txn ID (Amex Reference)
    provider_category TEXT,               -- bank's own category guess

    -- Our enrichment (filled by rules / manual / LLM later)
    category_id     INTEGER REFERENCES categories(id),
    tags            TEXT,                 -- JSON array
    notes           TEXT,

    -- Transfer pairing (set by a post-ingest reconciliation step)
    is_transfer     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    paired_id       INTEGER REFERENCES transactions(id),

    -- Lossless original row
    raw_json        TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE INDEX idx_tx_date         ON transactions(date);
CREATE INDEX idx_tx_account_date ON transactions(account_id, date);
CREATE INDEX idx_tx_category     ON transactions(category_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_tx_merchant     ON transactions(merchant);
CREATE INDEX idx_tx_amount       ON transactions(amount);
```

### `balance_snapshots`
Populated by the JSON sidecars (`<ts>_balance.json`) the credit-card scrapers already write. Also usable for periodic debit-account snapshots if we want net worth plotting later.

```sql
CREATE TABLE balance_snapshots (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    account_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    date        TEXT NOT NULL,            -- YYYY-MM-DD
    balance     REAL NOT NULL,            -- credit cards: + = currently owed
    source      TEXT NOT NULL,            -- 'scraper' | 'manual' | 'statement'
    raw         TEXT,                     -- original displayed text
    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    UNIQUE(account_id, date, source)
);
```

### `imports`
One row per ingest run per file. Audit + debug + protects against re-parsing the same CSV.

```sql
CREATE TABLE imports (
    id                   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    provider             TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_file          TEXT NOT NULL,
    imported_at          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    rows_read            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    transactions_added   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    transactions_skipped INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    status               TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'success' | 'error'
    error                TEXT
);

CREATE INDEX idx_imports_file     ON imports(source_file);
CREATE INDEX idx_imports_provider ON imports(provider);
```

### `category_rules`
Substring / regex / exact rules for auto-categorisation. Applied at ingest and re-runnable.

```sql
CREATE TABLE category_rules (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    pattern     TEXT NOT NULL,
    match_type  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'substring' CHECK (match_type IN ('substring','regex','exact')),
    field       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'description' CHECK (field IN ('description','merchant','counterparty')),
    category_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES categories(id),
    priority    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE INDEX idx_rules_priority ON category_rules(priority DESC);
```

### Notes on the design

- **Dedup hash**: SHA1 of `provider|account_label|date|amount|description` for most providers; for Amex use the `Reference` column as a more stable key. Function lives in `finance_db.py` so all parsers reuse it.
- **Sign flip for credit cards**: Barclaycard CSV has purchases as positive and payments as negative — flipped at ingest so `+ = into account` is the universal convention.
- **No CASCADE deletes** (matches fitness_db convention) — explicit cleanup if ever needed.
- **No splits, no recurring, no budgets, no goals** in v1. All are clean additive tables when wanted.

## Files to change

- **`argus/src/finance_db.py`** — REPLACE the current draft entirely. Add: schema above, `init_db()` with `executescript()` + seed inserts (accounts, categories), `dedup_hash()` helper, `upsert_account(provider, label, ...)` helper, `insert_transaction(...)` helper that returns `(id, was_new)`. Top-of-file docstring documents the design choices.

## Out of scope for this plan (future steps)

These are the layers that will sit on top of the schema, not part of designing the schema itself:

1. **One parser per provider** under `argus/scrapers/parse_<provider>.py` (or `argus/finance/parsers/`) — read CSV → yield transaction dicts.
2. **`ingest.py`** — walk `~/.argus/finance/raw/<provider>/` for any CSV not in `imports`, dispatch to the right parser, write transactions, write any sidecar `_balance.json` into `balance_snapshots`.
3. **Transfer pairing pass** — match `-X` and `+X` of equal amount across accounts within ±2 days, set `is_transfer=1` + `paired_id`.
4. **Categorisation pass** — apply `category_rules`; fall back to LLM classification later.
5. **Reports / dashboard** — likely a `finance_web/` Flask app mirroring `fitness_web/`.

## Verification

Once the schema lands:

```bash
cd /Users/sumeet/matrix/web/argus/argus
python -m src.finance_db                       # creates the DB at ~/.argus/finance/finance.db
sqlite3 ~/.argus/finance/finance.db ".schema"  # confirm all tables, indexes, constraints
sqlite3 ~/.argus/finance/finance.db "SELECT provider, label, account_type FROM accounts"
sqlite3 ~/.argus/finance/finance.db "SELECT id, name, parent_id FROM categories ORDER BY parent_id NULLS FIRST, sort_order"
```

Confirm:
- 5 seeded accounts (one per scraper provider).
- ~20 seeded categories with proper hierarchy.
- All FK / CHECK / UNIQUE constraints behave (try inserting a duplicate `(provider, label)` — should fail).
- Schema is idempotent — running `init_db()` twice doesn't error or duplicate seeds (use `INSERT OR IGNORE`).

Returns (id, was_new). If a row with the\n    same dedup_hash already exists, returns (existing_id, False).\n\n    Required keys: account_id, source_file, dedup_hash, date, amount,\n                   description, raw_json.\n    Optional: initiated_date, fee, balance_after, original_amount,\n              original_currency, merchant, counterparty, transaction_type,\n              reference, provider_category, category_id, tags, notes,\n              is_transfer, paired_id.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(tx.get(\"raw_json\"), (dict, list)):\n        tx[\"raw_json\"] = json.dumps(tx[\"raw_json\"], default=str)\n    if isinstance(tx.get(\"tags\"), (list, tuple)):\n        tx[\"tags\"] = json.dumps(list(tx[\"tags\"]))\n\n    cols = [\n        \"account_id\", \"source_file\", \"dedup_hash\",\n        \"date\", \"initiated_date\",\n        \"amount\", \"fee\", \"balance_after\",\n        \"original_amount\", \"original_currency\",\n        \"description\", \"merchant\", \"counterparty\",\n        \"transaction_type\", \"reference\", \"provider_category\",\n        \"category_id\", \"tags\", \"notes\",\n        \"is_transfer\", \"paired_id\",\n        \"raw_json\",\n    ]\n    placeholders = \", \".join(\"?\" for _ in cols)\n    sql = (\n        f\"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO transactions ({', '.join(cols)})\"\n        f\" VALUES ({placeholders})\"\n    )\n    values = [tx.get(c) for c in cols]\n    # Required cols can't be None.\n    for required in (\"account_id\", \"source_file\", \"dedup_hash\", \"date\", \"amount\", \"description\", \"raw_json\"):\n        if tx.get(required) is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"insert_transaction: missing required field {required!r}\")\n\n    cur = conn.execute(sql, values)\n    if cur.rowcount > 0:\n        return cur.lastrowid, True\n    existing = conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT id FROM transactions WHERE dedup_hash = ?\",\n        (tx[\"dedup_hash\"],),\n    ).fetchone()\n    return (existing[\"id\"] if existing else None), False\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    init_db()\n    print(f\"Initialised: {DB_PATH}\")\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/argus/argus/finance/parsers/amex.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Amex UK CSV parser.\n\nHeader row:\n    Date,Description,Amount,Extended Details,Appears On Your Statement As,\n    Address,Town/City,Postcode,Country,Reference,Category\n\nDate: DD/MM/YYYY.\nAmount: positive = purchase, negative = payment/refund (from card account\nperspective). We FLIP the sign so the universal convention holds:\n  + = into the card account (refund / payment to clear card)\n  - = out of the card account (purchase)\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Iterator\n\nPROVIDER = \"amex\"\nACCOUNT_TYPE = \"credit_card\"\n\n\ndef parse(path: Path) -> tuple[str, Iterator[dict]]:\n    return \"default\", _iter(path)\n\n\ndef _iter(path: Path) -> Iterator[dict]:\n    with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8-sig\") as f:\n        reader = csv.DictReader(f)\n        for row in reader:\n            try:\n                date = datetime.strptime(row[\"Date\"].strip(), \"%d/%m/%Y\").strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n            except (KeyError, ValueError):\n                continue\n            amount_raw = (row.get(\"Amount\") or \"\").strip()\n            if not amount_raw:\n                continue\n            amount = -float(amount_raw.replace(\",\", \"\"))  # flip sign\n\n            description = (row.get(\"Description\") or \"\").strip()\n            details = (row.get(\"Extended Details\") or \"\").strip()\n            reference = (row.get(\"Reference\") or \"\").strip() or None\n            provider_category = (row.get(\"Category\") or \"\").strip() or None\n\n            yield {\n                \"date\": date,\n                \"amount\": amount,\n                \"description\": description,\n                \"transaction_type\": None,\n                \"reference\": reference,\n                \"provider_category\": provider_category,\n                \"merchant\": _guess_merchant(row),\n                \"notes\": details if details and details != description else None,\n                \"raw\": dict(row),\n            }\n\n\ndef _guess_merchant(row: dict) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Amex's \"Appears On Your Statement As\" is usually a cleaner form than\n    the raw description.\"\"\"\n    v = (row.get(\"Appears On Your Statement As\") or \"\").strip()\n    return v or None\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/sumeet/matrix/web/argus/argus/finance/parsers/barclaycard.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Barclaycard CSV parser.\n\nNo header row. Columns:\n    0: Date       — \"DD MMM YY\" (e.g. \"10 May 26\")\n    1: Description (quoted, with leading/trailing spaces)\n    2: Card type   (\"Visa\" / \"n/a\")\n    3: Card holder\n    4: Provider category (\"Shopping\" etc.)\n    5: Negative amount column (used for payments/credits, e.g. \"-359.17\")\n    6: Positive amount column (used for purchases, e.g. \"16.10\")\n\nSign convention: column 5 is already negative (payment from your bank to the\ncard account); column 6 is positive (purchase = money out of card account).\nWe FLIP both so + means into the card account, - means out:\n    purchase 16.10  → amount = -16.10\n    payment -359.17 → amount = +359.17\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Iterator\n\nPROVIDER = \"barclaycard\"\nACCOUNT_TYPE = \"credit_card\"\n\n\ndef parse(path: Path) -> tuple[str, Iterator[dict]]:\n    return \"default\", _iter(path)\n\n\ndef _iter(path: Path) -> Iterator[dict]:\n    with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8-sig\") as f:\n        reader = csv.reader(f)\n        for row in reader:\n            if len(row) < 7:\n                continue\n            try:\n                date = datetime.strptime(row[0].strip(), \"%d %b %y\").strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n            except ValueError:\n                continue\n            description = row[1].strip().strip(\",\").strip()\n            card_type = row[2].strip() or None\n            provider_category = (row[4] or \"\").strip() or None\n\n            neg = (row[5] or \"\").strip()\n            pos = (row[6] or \"\").strip()\n            if pos:\n                amount = -float(pos.replace(\",\", \"\"))  # purchase → out of account\n            elif neg:\n                amount = -float(neg.replace(\",\", \"\"))  # already negative → flip to positive\n            else:\n                continue\n\n            yield {\n                \"date\": date,\n                \"amount\": amount,\n                \"description\": description,\n                \"transaction_type\": card_type,\n                \"provider_category\": provider_category,\n                \"raw\": {\n                    \"date\": row[0], \"description\": row[1], \"card_type\": row[2],\n                    \"card_holder\": row[3], \"category\": row[4],\n                    \"neg_amount\": row[5], \"pos_amount\": row[6],\n                },\n            }\n"
}
